chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Fadl ibn Kathir al-Madani, from Sa'd ibn Abi Sa'id al-Balkhi, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying:

Indeed, for Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, there is a prayer in every time which a pray-er prays; Allah sends mercy upon His believing servants and those who hold fast [to faith], and among this creation He curses them. He was asked: 'I am your ransom, and why?' He replied: 'Because of their denial of our rights and their falsifying us.'

key_terms.حَقَّنَا: Our rights (referring to the rights of the Imams/Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.صَلَاهً: Prayer (specifically a time or occasion for divine action)

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah curse those who deny the rights of the Imams?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, the Imam elucidates the dual nature of divine decree, where specific times are designated for either mercy or curse based on the believers' recognition of the Ahl al-Bayt. The curse is specifically attributed to the denial of the Imams' rights (*Haqquna*) and the rejection of their truth, highlighting the theological weight of *Wilayah* in determining spiritual fate. This underscores the Shia concept that enmity toward the Imams is not merely a social slight but a fundamental rejection of divine authority.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 8.  It is narrated that Imam Musa Kadhim (a.s.) said, “Just as Allah,  the  Mighty  and  Sublime  showers  mercy  on  His believing  servants  at  the  time  of  Prayers,  He  also  curses some  people.”
He  was  asked,  “Why  are  some  people cursed?”  He  replied,  “Because  they  deny  our  rights  and falsify us.”
